newsitem.title: GERMANY: German press sees French vote changing Europe.
newsitem.headline: German press sees French vote changing Europe.

text.p: German newspapers voiced concern on Monday about the future of Europe's integration drive, and especially its planned common currency, after the Socialist-led left won the French parliamentary election.

Several commentaries noted the turn to the left in France, Germany's most important partner, was leaving Christian Democratic Chancellor Helmut Kohl increasingly isolated at a crucial time in the run-up to Europe's monetary union (EMU).
"The election has changed not only the political face of France, but also that of Europe," the Frankfurter Rundschau wrote.

"Of the 15 European Union members, 12 are governed by or with the left, which does not want any more austerity for the euro in view of the social problems involved. For Bonn, it will be more difficult to push through 'pure Maastricht'."

The business daily Handelsblatt said the prime minister-elect, Socialist party leader Lionel Jospin, wanted to end the liberal reforms pursued by his predecessor Alain Juppe and redirect economic policy towards boosting domestic demand.
"If one takes his campaign statements at face value, France can get ready for an archaic economic policy and Germany can expect a livelier debate about the euro," it wrote.

"The Bonn government will have to adjust to the fact that Paris will in future place more emphasis on growth than on trimming its budget and will question the European stability pact in its present form.

"There is no need for panic reactions in Bonn, but the politicians east of the Rhine will have to think about how they will react to the changed priorities of their most important partner. They had better do it quickly."
Bonn's General-Anzeiger newspaper said the election was a slap in the face for President Jacques Chirac, who was now "one size smaller in political terms."

"As a partner, he will be more difficult than ever," the daily wrote. "An uncertain leader who wants to make up for a mistake has to be handled with caution. Europe could be the next laboratory for Chirac's experiments.
"Chirac will try to talk with Kohl about changing the criteria for the stability pact and for joining the Euro-club," it wrote. "If need be, one will have to delay the Euro-era a bit."
The Saarbruecker Zeitung said "the signs in Europe are pointing to a storm."
The Neue Osnabruecker Zeitung said the domestic political balance was changing in Europe.

"First the Labour triumph in Britain, now the victory of the left in France -- two of the most important EU countries have voted for change," it wrote. "Social concerns play a dominant role at a time of austerity...This is a clear warning sign to the Bonn coalition, which should not ignore it if it does not want to damage itself."
